newsitem.title: CANADA: FX industry moves to cope with EMU, not stymie it.
newsitem.headline: FX industry moves to cope with EMU, not stymie it.

text.p: Few foreign exchange market professionals at this year's annual ACI gathering expressed any love for European monetary union (EMU), but the industry debate has shifted decisively to how to cope with the single currency and less of how to avoid it.

Apart from the political momentum that has built up for a punctual start to EMU in 1999, foreign exchange dealers from around the globe are acutely aware of the huge resources the banking industry and trade associations have already invested in facilitating the project.

At a fringe meeting at the ACI's 39th annual congress in Toronto late Friday, speakers discussed details of the preparations for the currency switchover that are being made in settlements and payments, market conventions and technological adjustments.

"I personally have no doubt the euro will come into being on January 1, 1999. It's a political decision and to some extent its a bureaucratic issue," said Bob Blower, assistant director in charge of foreign exchange and money markets at the British Bankers Association (BBA).

"When a decision as big as this is made, a huge momentum builds up bureaucratically to the extent that there are now an awful lot of people whose jobs now depend on EMU going ahead," said Blower. "There is a tremendous head of steam pushing this ahead."
Blower said UK banks already were fairly well prepared for the event and European continental banks even more so.
Organizations like the BBA and the ACI are currently working on ways of harmonizing market practices after EMU and ironing out the outstanding creases.
The areas being closely monitored are things like standardizing international day counts, market holidays, settlements practices and legal conventions.

The BBA, for example, recommended using 360 days as the benchmark year for cash and derivatives and publishing a London Interbank Offered Rate (Libor) for the new euro that would replace existing national currency Libors. It also recommended a spot basis for settlements.

The ACI, meantime, has set up a committee on the euro to examine similar post-EMU details. This group, which is assuming the 15 European Union states will be affected, has been recognized by the European Monetary Institute.
Senior dealers said there was still a outside chance of a delay to EMU but this was less likely, and preparations had to continue apace.

"EMU is not an economic event, it is a political event. It should be an economic event but that does not change the reality," said David Clark, head of foreign exchange at Bankgesellschaft Berlin and honorary president of the ACI.

"There are some market participants outside of Europe who think EMU is still some sort of fantasy and I can only hope this will this will not prevent them taking necessary precautions," said Clark, who estimated that 60 percent of forex players were now certain of EMU going ahead.

An illustration of that mood of inevitability was seen in a Reuters poll of dealers attending the Toronto ACI meeting that showed just two out of 15 believed the recent row between the Bundesbank and German government over the revaluation of Germany's gold reserves would materially alter the EMU timetable.

Even Bundesbank board member Wendelin Hartmann, also speaking at the ACI meeting on Friday, said he thought it would be wrong now to delay EMU even though he frowned on the plan to revalue gold in order to met the entry criteria.

"The Bundesbank feels obliged to make these noises as a sort of guardian of the process, but the Bundesbank are civil servants and really don't have the final say here," said a senior foreign exchange dealer at a French bank in New York.
Economic short cuts for political expediency would come at a price, however.
Dealers expected the initial months at least of the euro to be turbulent.

"It's highly unlikely the euro is going to be a stable currency from day one. It's going to be a very volatile time and how the European central bank copes with this tricky period will be crucial," said Bankgesellschaft's Clark.
